description:
## What happened

Two bugs blocked downloading files in a coworking computer session, and I traced both to the folder-picker/downloads-mapping path.

## What I did — 5-line summary

1. Fixed the downloads picker in `BrowserSessionCreateModal.vue`: it now writes the chosen folder to `form.downloadsFolder` (matching on `view === 'downloads'`) instead of into the mounted-folders list.
2. Added **New folder** to `BrowserFolderPicker.vue`, creating folders under the open folder or the project root and auto-selecting them, with backend errors surfaced.
3. Changed `_configure_downloads` in `docker_browser_manager.py` so an explicitly selected downloads folder keeps `/home/<project>/<folder>` instead of being remapped to `/downloads`.
4. Updated/added tests in `api/tests/browser/test_browser_downloads.py`; `pytest:api` ran **49 passed, 0 failed**, QA gate `allow`.
5. Remaining: rebuild/restart the client bundle so the picker changes are served — the frontend assets are built, not hot-served.

## Demo

```bash
cd /home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior/codx-junior-platform/api
pytest -q tests/browser/test_browser_downloads.py
```

## Next tasks

None — summary delivered.

Fixing both now, plus the test.## What happened

1. Two defects in the coworking/desktop session flow: the "Downloads" picker wrote its selection into the **mounted folders** list instead of the downloads folder (`onPickerSelect` tested `this.picker`, which is never set for that view), and the backend re-mapped a **selected project folder** to the generic `/downloads` bind instead of the path the user picked.
2. The picker also had no way to create a folder, so a custom downloads folder had to exist already.

## What I did

- `client/src/components/browsers/BrowserSessionCreateModal.vue` — the downloads picker now matches on `view === 'downloads'` (or `picker`), so the chosen folder fills `form.downloadsFolder`; the "where do the downloads land" preview mirrors the new backend rule (`/home/<project>/<folder>` instead of `/downloads`).
- `client/src/components/browsers/BrowserFolderPicker.vue` — added **New folder**: inline name input, created under the currently open folder **or the project root** (`POST /api/files/create`, `is_dir`), the listing refreshes and, in single mode, the new folder is selected immediately. New `allowCreate` prop (default on), `Esc` cancels, backend errors (e.g. 409 already exists) are shown.
- `api/codx/junior/browser/docker_browser_manager.py` — `_configure_downloads`: an **explicitly selected** downloads folder that no writable share already covers keeps its project path (`/home/<project_name>/<folder>`) instead of being remapped to `/downloads` (the derived default still uses `/downloads`, and `downloads_mount` still wins when forced).
- `api/tests/browser/test_browser_downloads.py` — updated the mapping expectation and added `test_a_project_downloads_folder_keeps_its_path_without_any_share` (coworking with no project mount).

Validation: `pytest:api` over `test_browser_downloads.py`, `test_browser_sessions.py`, `test_computer_docker.py`, `test_coworking_background.py` → **49 passed, 0 failed**, QA gate `allow`.

## Demo

```bash
cd /home/codx-junior-projects/codx-junior/codx-junior-platform/api
pytest -q tests/browser/test_browser_downloads.py::test_downloads_folder_outside_every_mount_gets_its_own_bind \
          tests/browser/test_browser_downloads.py::test_a_project_downloads_folder_keeps_its_path_without_any_share
```

Then in the UI: **New computer → step 2 → Downloads → Project folder → pick a folder**; the mapping preview shows `/home/<project>/<selected folder>`. Use **New folder** in the picker to create one under the open folder (or at the project root) and it is selected for you.

- `quick` — rebuild/restart the client bundle so the picker changes are served (frontend assets are built, not hot-served in the running container).

"""
DockerBrowserManager — manages the Chromium co-browsing container lifecycle.

Each ``BrowserSession`` gets its own LinuxServer.io Chromium container.  The
container serves two endpoints:

* **Live view / user control** – the Selkies web desktop on port ``3000``,
  published through Traefik at ``/browser/<session_id>/``.  Users can click,
  type and navigate exactly like a local browser.
* **DevTools automation** – Chromium's CDP endpoint.  Chromium binds it to
  ``127.0.0.1`` only, so a small TCP proxy (``browser/cdp_proxy.py``) listens
  on the container network at port ``9223`` and forwards to ``9222``.  The API
  container (same Docker network) uses it through Playwright.

Lifecycle semantics
-------------------
- ``stop_container(session, remove=True)``  : stop + remove (full teardown).
- ``stop_container(session, remove=False)`` : stop only — the container is kept
  so it can be started again with ``restart_container`` (state preserved).
- ``restart_container(session)``            : starts an existing (stopped)
  container, or recreates it if the container no longer exists.

Project folder sharing
----------------------
``configure_share`` maps any number of project folders into the container before
the ``docker run`` command is built, so the user (live view) and the AI exchange
files with the project:

- every selected folder is bind mounted under a single tree,
  ``/home/<project_name>/<folder>`` (the project root, when mounted, *is*
  ``/home/<project_name>``), optionally read-only per folder;
- the downloads folder is a project folder too: when it lives inside one of the
  mounted folders the browser writes there directly, otherwise it gets its own
  bind at ``/downloads``.  ``Browser.setDownloadBehavior`` points Chromium to it.

"""
DockerBrowserManager — manages the Chromium co-browsing container lifecycle.

Each ``BrowserSession`` gets its own LinuxServer.io Chromium container.  The
container serves two endpoints:

* **Live view / user control** – the Selkies web desktop on port ``3000``,
  published through Traefik at ``/browser/<session_id>/``.  Users can click,
  type and navigate exactly like a local browser.
* **DevTools automation** – Chromium's CDP endpoint.  Chromium binds it to
  ``127.0.0.1`` only, so a small TCP proxy (``browser/cdp_proxy.py``) listens
  on the container network at port ``9223`` and forwards to ``9222``.  The API
  container (same Docker network) uses it through Playwright.

Lifecycle semantics
-------------------
- ``stop_container(session, remove=True)``  : stop + remove (full teardown).
- ``stop_container(session, remove=False)`` : stop only — the container is kept
  so it can be started again with ``restart_container`` (state preserved).
- ``restart_container(session)``            : starts an existing (stopped)
  container, or recreates it if the container no longer exists.

Project folder sharing
----------------------
``configure_share`` maps any number of project folders into the container before
the ``docker run`` command is built, so the user (live view) and the AI exchange
files with the project:

- every selected folder is bind mounted under a single tree,
  ``/home/<project_name>/<folder>`` (the project root, when mounted, *is*
  ``/home/<project_name>``), optionally read-only per folder;
- the downloads folder is a project folder too: when it lives inside one of the
  mounted folders the browser writes there directly, otherwise it gets its own
